term: one nonfunctional law with lawful alternatives
definition: relationalLaw c a is the implication c.2=true → a=true. When a constraint is imposed only true is lawful; when absent, false and true are both lawful at the very same input under this single relation. Nonfunctionality is not failure to obey the relation. No stochastic dynamics, probabilities, physical realization, agent control or moral responsibility are represented.
note: Analyst-defined control motivated by the Carneades definition fork; no source attribution. Adequacy and applicability remain open. See docs/notes/carneades-choice-context.md.
